blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A global team is not, despite appearances, a collection of nationalities. It is a collection of individuals whose professional habits, expectations and communication instincts were quietly shaped by cultures they themselves often cannot describe. The leader's task is not to memorise cultural stereotypes, but to remain curious, observant and willing to be corrected by the individuals in front of them.

There are, however, useful patterns to be aware of. Some cultures treat silence as a space for thought, others as a sign of disagreement. Some see a direct "no" as a mark of honesty, others as an act of aggression. A leader who can read which pattern is at work in a given meeting, without reducing anyone to a caricature, will consistently get more from their team than one who cannot.

Language, notwithstanding its universality on the surface, behaves differently across cultures. British understatement — "it could be worse", meaning "we are in a crisis" — is genuinely confusing for colleagues from cultures where language means what it says. Great global leaders learn to notice when their words are landing in a register different from the one they intended, and to clarify quickly, without embarrassment on either side.

items.q: According to the text, what is a global team, fundamentally?
options: A group defined by its shared language
A collection of nationalities
A set of cultural stereotypes
A collection of individuals shaped by cultures they cannot always describe
items.why: "It is a collection of individuals whose professional habits… were quietly shaped by cultures they themselves often cannot describe."

items.q: How may silence function differently across cultures, according to the text?
options: Always as a sign of respect
As a space for thought in some, a sign of disagreement in others
Only as a sign of boredom
As an act of aggression everywhere
items.why: "Some cultures treat silence as a space for thought, others as a sign of disagreement."

items.q: What does the example "it could be worse" meaning "we are in a crisis" illustrate?
options: That crises should be hidden from the team
That English is universal
That honesty is culturally identical everywhere
That British understatement can genuinely confuse direct communicators
items.why: É o exemplo do understatement britânico, que confunde quem lê a língua ao pé da letra.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Leaders should stay curious and willing to be corrected
Memorising a fixed list of cultural stereotypes is the key to leading global teams
Meaning can travel differently even when the language is shared
A single "no" can mean honesty in one culture and aggression in another
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita a memorização de estereótipos — o que vale é curiosidade e observação do indivíduo.

items.q: The phrase "without reducing anyone to a caricature" suggests that the author believes…
options: patterns are useful only if they do not flatten the individual
leaders should avoid noticing cultural differences
every colleague behaves exactly as their culture predicts
cultural patterns should be ignored entirely
items.why: Inferência: os padrões ajudam, mas a pessoa nunca deve ser reduzida a uma caricatura do seu grupo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James em uma conversa individual com um colega da equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time, Priya. I schedule these one-to-ones for a fairly selfish reason: with seven nationalities in the room, I genuinely cannot tell how my words are landing, and the group meeting hides that from me.

Yesterday, when I said the first draft was "not quite there yet", I meant it warmly — it was, honestly, very close. But I have been burned before. British understatement can read as devastating criticism to someone who takes language at face value, and the last thing I want is for the team to walk away deflated over a compliment.

So, two things. Tell me candidly whether my feedback ever sounds harsher, or softer, than I intend. And when silence falls in a meeting, help me read it — because I honestly cannot tell whether people are thinking, disagreeing, or simply waiting for someone senior to speak first.

My promise to you is this: if I ever misread the room, correct me on the spot. I would far rather clarify in the moment than let a small misunderstanding quietly harden into resentment.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does James schedule these one-to-one conversations?
options: To assign extra work privately
Because he prefers not to meet as a group
Because the group meeting hides how his words are landing
To evaluate each colleague's performance formally
items.why: "the group meeting hides that from me" — o encontro em grupo esconde como as palavras dele soam.

items.q: What did James actually mean when he called the first draft "not quite there yet"?
options: That it was, honestly, very close
That it was a serious failure
That he had not read it
That it needed to be started again
items.why: "I meant it warmly — it was, honestly, very close."

items.q: What does James ask Priya to help him do about silence in meetings?
options: Record who stays quiet
Ignore it completely
Read whether it signals thought, disagreement, or deference
Fill it by speaking first
items.why: Ele não sabe se o silêncio é reflexão, discordância ou espera pelo sênior — pede ajuda para lê-lo.

items.q: What does James imply by saying "I have been burned before"?
options: He dislikes giving any feedback at all
He once lost a major client
A past understatement of his was badly misread
He was formally reprimanded by leadership
items.why: Inferência: a experiência anterior foi um eufemismo mal interpretado como crítica devastadora.

items.q: What does James's promise to be corrected "on the spot" reveal about his approach?
options: He values speed of delivery above all
He prefers to address problems only in writing
He treats clarifying early as better than letting misunderstandings harden
He expects colleagues to adapt entirely to him
items.why: Inferência: ele prefere esclarecer na hora a deixar um mal-entendido virar ressentimento.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "His email was pure understatement: 'a minor hiccup' turned out to be a system-wide outage." An understatement is…
options: a description that deliberately makes something sound less serious than it is
a formal written apology
a factual, neutral report
an exaggeration for effect
items.why: Understatement = eufemismo: descrever algo como menos grave do que realmente é.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Her feedback was accurate, but the harsh ___ made the team feel attacked rather than helped."
options: sensibility
register
nuance
caricature
items.why: Register = registro: o tom/nível de formalidade em que a mensagem é transmitida.

items.q: "In a high-context culture, much of the message lives in what is left unsaid." This describes a culture where…
options: written contracts replace all conversation
everything must be stated explicitly
meaning relies heavily on context, relationships and the unspoken
hierarchy is irrelevant
items.why: Cultura de alto contexto: grande parte do sentido está no implícito e no contexto, não nas palavras literais.

items.q: "Assuming every German colleague is blunt reduces a whole nation to a caricature." A caricature is…
options: an exaggerated, oversimplified image of someone or a group
an official job description
a balanced, detailed portrait
a neutral statistical average
items.why: Caricature = caricatura: imagem exagerada e simplista que achata a pessoa ou o grupo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Practising ___ means assuming the other person meant something reasonable before assuming they meant offence."
options: interpretive charity
low-context culture
global sensibility
understatement
items.why: Interpretive charity = caridade interpretativa: presumir a intenção razoável antes de presumir a ofensa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na liderança de equipes globais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "A good global leader learns to read the room before pushing a decision." To read the room means to…
options: read documents aloud to the group
check who is physically in attendance
review the meeting minutes
sense the mood and unspoken reactions of the people present
items.why: Read the room = ler o ambiente: perceber o clima e as reações não ditas dos presentes.

items.q: "When his joke fell flat, he stopped to clear up the misunderstanding at once." To clear up means to…
options: tidy the meeting room
end the meeting early
cancel the discussion
resolve or explain something that was confusing
items.why: Clear up = esclarecer, resolver um mal-entendido — alinhado ao 'clarify quickly' da lição.

items.q: "Two colleagues quietly pushed back on the deadline, though no one said a firm 'no'." They…
options: resisted or gently challenged it
accepted it immediately
moved the deadline forward
forgot about it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar de forma comedida — sem um 'não' explícito.

items.q: "Let's not talk past each other — I think we actually agree." To talk past each other means to…
options: interrupt the chairperson
argue loudly in public
agree without discussion
fail to understand one another despite both speaking
items.why: Talk past each other = falar sem se entender: cada um segue seu ponto sem realmente se conectar.

items.q: "Give people the benefit of the doubt before assuming they meant offence." This means to…
options: ask for written confirmation of everything
assume the worst until proven otherwise
avoid working with them
trust that their intention was reasonable when the evidence is unclear
items.why: Give the benefit of the doubt = dar o benefício da dúvida — a versão idiomática da 'interpretive charity' da lição.
